methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $80M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
CarbonCapture Inc., a Series B climate and energy technology company founded by Adrian Corless, has raised $80M to date. The relevant peer universe consists of nine private companies and one public comparable (LNZA), all operating in climate technology and adjacent energy infrastructure sectors.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach uses total capital raised as a proxy baseline, applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-subsequent-stage advancement, yielding $152M. The peer-median method examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C). The median of this peer set is $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B.

Triangulation across these two methods produces a valuation range of $129M (low), $576M (median), and $1.1B (high). The wide spread reflects material uncertainty in stage-comparable selection and the heterogeneity of peer business models within climate tech. The peer-median method implies significantly higher value than stage progression, suggesting either CarbonCapture commands above-median status within its peer cohort or that Series C comparables may not fully reflect Series B risk. Key sensitivities include revenue traction relative to peer benchmarks and capital efficiency metrics, which are not present in current data.
